situation:
You are the operations manager at CLEARBROOK HOME CLEANING, a residential cleaning franchise with two branches and about ninety cleaners. The new president (judge), brought in after two losing years, has asked you to recommend whether a practice used at one branch should become the standard at both.

The north branch has cleared its damage claims and returned to profit. Its crews record a short video walkthrough of each home at arrival and departure, which settles disputes over broken items in a day. The service agreement customers sign permits the recording, and no one has had to explain it to them.

The south branch does not record, and its unresolved claims are most of what the company still loses. Its cleaners say cameras would tell them they are not trusted, and several would leave. Customers who understood what the agreement permits would object, though the company is within its rights. Ending the practice everywhere gives back the savings that returned the north branch to profit.

The president (judge) wants you to recommend one standard for both branches and to say how it would be communicated to the cleaners. You will present in the president's (judge) office. The president (judge) will begin by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas, and will thank you for your work after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the president (judge) of CLEARBROOK HOME CLEANING, brought in after two losing years to return the franchise to profit. Business background is the same as the situation above. The two branches now work differently, and you have to name one standard before the spring hiring round.

You want the operations manager to recommend one standard for both branches and to say how that decision would be communicated to the cleaners.

During the presentation you are to ask the following questions of the participant:
judgeQuestions: What would the course you did not choose have cost us?
